findings.name: shop-api
findings.message: The manifest sets no namespace, so the object goes to the namespace of the current context, which is often default.
findings.fix: Set metadata.namespace, or apply the files with a namespace on the command line and keep that in the pipeline.

manual.quote: For a production cluster, consider not using the default namespace. Instead, make other namespaces and use those.

findings.name: shop-api
findings.message: The Deployment runs one replica, and no PodDisruptionBudget in the files selects its Pods. A voluntary disruption, such as draining a node, takes the only Pod down.
findings.fix: Run two or more replicas and add a PodDisruptionBudget, or accept the downtime on purpose.

manual.quote: As an application owner, you can create a PodDisruptionBudget (PDB) for each application. A PDB limits the number of Pods of a replicated application that are down simultaneously from voluntary disruptions.
Replicate your application if you need higher availability.

manual.page: Specifying a Disruption Budget for your Application
manual.section: Think about how your application reacts to disruptions
manual.quote: Possible Solution 1: Do not use a PDB and tolerate occasional downtime.

manual.page: Specifying a Disruption Budget for your Application
manual.quote: In this case, make a note of the controller's .spec.selector; the same selector goes into the PDBs .spec.selector.

findings.name: shop-api
findings.message: hostNetwork is true, so the Pod shares the host's namespace. The Baseline profile of the Pod Security Standards disallows it.
findings.fix: Remove hostNetwork, or set it to false.

manual.quote: Sharing the host namespaces must be disallowed.

findings.name: shop-api
findings.message: The container has no resource request for cpu and memory. The scheduler cannot place it by what it needs, and the node can evict it first when memory runs short.
findings.fix: Set resources.requests.cpu and resources.requests.memory to what the container uses in normal work.

manual.page: Resource Management for Pods and Containers
manual.section: Resource Management for Pods and Containers
manual.quote: When you specify the resource request for containers in a Pod, the kube-scheduler uses this information to decide which node to place the Pod on.

manual.page: Resource Management for Pods and Containers
manual.section: How Pods with resource requests are scheduled
manual.quote: The scheduler ensures that, for each resource type, the sum of the resource requests of the scheduled containers is less than the capacity of the node.

manual.page: Resource Management for Pods and Containers
manual.section: How Kubernetes applies resource requests and limits
manual.quote: If a container exceeds its memory request and the node that it runs on becomes short of memory overall, it is likely that the Pod the container belongs to will be evicted.

findings.name: shop-api
findings.message: The container has no resource limit for cpu and memory, so nothing stops it from using more of it than it asked for.
findings.fix: Set resources.limits.memory (and resources.limits.cpu if you want a ceiling on CPU).

manual.page: Resource Management for Pods and Containers
manual.section: Resource Management for Pods and Containers
manual.quote: When you specify a resource limit for a container, the kubelet enforces those limits so that the running container is not allowed to use more of that resource than the limit you set.

manual.page: Resource Management for Pods and Containers
manual.quote: memory limits are enforced by the kernel with out of memory (OOM) kills.

manual.page: Resource Management for Pods and Containers
manual.quote: cpu limits are enforced by CPU throttling.

findings.name: shop-api
findings.message: The container has no readinessProbe (it has a livenessProbe, which does not wait for readiness), so the Pod receives traffic as soon as it starts, before the application can answer.
findings.fix: Add a readinessProbe (httpGet, tcpSocket, grpc or exec) that succeeds only when the application can answer.

manual.quote: Readiness probes determine when a container is ready to accept traffic.

manual.section: When should you use a readiness probe?
manual.quote: To start sending traffic to a Pod only when a probe succeeds, specify a readiness probe.
If the readiness probe returns a failed state, the EndpointSlice controller removes the Pod's IP address from the EndpointSlices of all Services that match the Pod.
Liveness probes do not wait for readiness probes to succeed.

findings.name: shop-api
findings.message: The image registry.example/shop/api:latest uses the tag latest. Kubernetes cannot tell which version of the image is running, and a rollback does not return to the version before.
findings.fix: Use a tag that names a version, or the digest of the image (name@sha256:...).

manual.quote: You should avoid using the :latest tag when deploying containers in production as it is harder to track which version of the image is running and more difficult to roll back properly.
Instead, specify a meaningful tag such as v1.42.0 and/or a digest.
if you omit the imagePullPolicy field, and the tag for the container image is :latest, imagePullPolicy is automatically set to Always.
An image digest uniquely identifies a specific version of the image, so Kubernetes runs the same code every time it starts a container with that image name and digest specified.

findings.name: shop-api
findings.message: The container binds the port of the node 8080 with hostPort. The Baseline profile of the Pod Security Standards says host ports should be disallowed entirely, or restricted to a known list.
findings.fix: Remove hostPort and reach the container through a Service.

manual.quote: HostPorts should be disallowed entirely (recommended) or restricted to a known list

findings.name: shop-api
findings.message: The environment variable DATABASE_PASSWORD is written in the manifest with a plain value, and its name says it holds a secret. The value is not shown here.
findings.fix: Keep the value in a Secret and read it with valueFrom.secretKeyRef.

manual.quote: A Secret is an object that contains a small amount of sensitive data such as a password, a token, or a key. Such information might otherwise be put in a Pod specification or in a container image.
Because Secrets can be created independently of the Pods that use them, there is less risk of the Secret (and its data) being exposed during the workflow of creating, viewing, and editing Pods.
For each container in your Pod specification, add an environment variable for each Secret key that you want to use to the env[].valueFrom.secretKeyRef field.

findings.name: shop-api
findings.message: allowPrivilegeEscalation is not set to false. The Restricted profile of the Pod Security Standards allows only false.
findings.fix: Set securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation to false.

manual.quote: Privilege escalation (such as via set-user-ID or set-group-ID file mode) should not be allowed.

findings.name: shop-api
findings.message: runAsNonRoot is not set to true, on the container or on the Pod. The Restricted profile of the Pod Security Standards requires containers to run as non-root users.
findings.fix: Set securityContext.runAsNonRoot to true, on the container or on the Pod, and make sure the image runs as a user other than root.

manual.quote: Containers must be required to run as non-root users.
The container fields may be undefined/nil if the pod-level spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot is set to true.

findings.name: shop-api
findings.message: No seccomp profile is set, on the container or on the Pod. The Restricted profile of the Pod Security Standards says that the absence of a profile is prohibited.
findings.fix: Set securityContext.seccompProfile.type to RuntimeDefault (or Localhost).

manual.quote: Seccomp profile must be explicitly set to one of the allowed values. Both the Unconfined profile and the absence of a profile are prohibited.
The container fields may be undefined/nil if the pod-level spec.securityContext.seccompProfile.type field is set appropriately.

findings.name: shop-api
findings.message: The container runs privileged. The Baseline profile of the Pod Security Standards disallows it.
findings.fix: Remove privileged, or set it to false, and add only the capabilities the container needs.

manual.quote: Privileged Pods disable most security mechanisms and must be disallowed.
If any of the listed containers fails to meet the requirements, the entire pod will fail validation.

findings.name: shop-api
findings.message: The container does not drop ALL capabilities. The Restricted profile of the Pod Security Standards says containers must drop ALL capabilities.
findings.fix: Set securityContext.capabilities.drop to [ALL], and add back only what the container needs.

manual.quote: Containers must drop ALL capabilities, and are only permitted to add back the NET_BIND_SERVICE capability.

findings.name: shop-api
findings.message: The container adds SYS_ADMIN, which the Baseline profile of the Pod Security Standards does not list among the capabilities that may be added.
findings.fix: Remove these capabilities, or run the workload in a namespace that enforces the Privileged profile on purpose.

manual.quote: Adding additional capabilities beyond those listed below must be disallowed.

findings.name: shop-api
findings.message: The image registry.example/shop/log-shipper has no tag and no digest, so Kubernetes uses the tag latest.
findings.fix: Use a tag that names a version, or the digest of the image (name@sha256:...).

manual.quote: If you don't specify a tag, Kubernetes assumes you mean the tag latest.
You should avoid using the :latest tag when deploying containers in production as it is harder to track which version of the image is running and more difficult to roll back properly.
if you omit the imagePullPolicy field, and you don't specify the tag for the container image, imagePullPolicy is automatically set to Always.
Instead, specify a meaningful tag such as v1.42.0 and/or a digest.

Digests are a unique identifier for a specific version of an image. Digests are hashes of the image's content, and are immutable. Tags can be moved to point to different images, but digests are fixed.

findings.name: shop-worker
findings.message: runAsUser of the Pod is 0, which is root. The Restricted profile of the Pod Security Standards does not allow it.
findings.fix: Set runAsUser to a user id above 0.

manual.quote: Containers must not set runAsUser to 0

findings.name: shop-worker
findings.message: The volume spool is a hostPath volume, which mounts a path of the node into the Pod. The Baseline profile of the Pod Security Standards forbids it.
findings.fix: Use a persistentVolumeClaim, a configMap, a secret or an emptyDir instead of a path of the node.

manual.quote: HostPath volumes must be forbidden.
